title: The Springs Behind a Running Bird
paras: Watching an [[ostrich|ostrich]] run across open grassland can reveal something surprising about sport: speed depends partly on recycling energy. Although this bird is not a [[mammal|mammal]], its legs share an important feature with those of human runners. Long tendons act like springs, storing energy when the foot lands and releasing it as the body moves forward.

Muscles [[occupy|occupy]] relatively little space near the bird's feet; much of their mass sits higher up the legs. This arrangement keeps the lower limbs light, so swinging them requires less effort. The bird's [[genetic|genetic]] inheritance guides the development of this body plan. However, good [[nutrition|nutrition]] is also necessary for building strong tissues, especially while a young bird is growing.

These biological springs require constant [[maintenance|maintenance]]. In living tendons, cells support the [[creation|creation]] of new protein fibres and remove damaged material. Unlike fallen leaves, which gradually [[decay|decay]], healthy tissue is continually renewed. Repair is not instant, however, which helps explain why repeated heavy exercise without enough recovery can injure a human runner's tendons.

For a runner reading about tendons in a [[quarterly|quarterly]] sports science magazine, this could be a reason to reconsider recovery time between runs. Running may have a [[spiritual|spiritual]] value beyond competition, but even someone seeking that inner peace depends on a physical mechanism shared with a flightless bird: each landing helps power the next stride.
zh: 观察鸵鸟在开阔的草地上奔跑，可以发现一个与运动有关的有趣事实：速度在一定程度上取决于能量的循环利用。虽然鸵鸟不是哺乳动物，但它的腿与人类跑者的腿有一个重要的共同点。长长的肌腱就像弹簧，在脚落地时储存能量，并在身体向前移动时释放能量。
鸵鸟脚部附近的肌肉占据的空间相对较小，大部分肌肉集中在腿部较高的位置。这种布局使小腿保持轻巧，因此摆动起来更省力。遗传因素引导着这种身体结构的发育。不过，良好的营养摄取也是构建强韧组织的必要条件，尤其是在幼鸟生长期间。
这些生物弹簧需要持续维护。在活体肌腱中，细胞帮助形成新的蛋白质纤维，并清除受损物质。落叶会逐渐腐烂，而健康的组织则不断更新。然而，修复并非即时完成，这也有助于解释为什么反复进行高强度运动却没有充分恢复，可能损伤人类跑者的肌腱。
对于在体育科学季刊中阅读肌腱相关内容的跑者来说，这可能成为重新考虑两次跑步之间恢复时间的一个理由。跑步或许具有超越竞技的心灵价值，但即使是寻求这种内心平静的人，也依赖一种与不会飞的鸟类共有的物理机制：每次落地，都在为下一步提供动力。

q.s: Both ostriches and human runners have tendons that can store and return energy.
q.why: 首段说明两者的肌腱都像弹簧储存并释放能量。

q.s: Young ostriches need more protein each day than adult ostriches.
q.why: 文章未比较幼鸟与成年鸵鸟的每日蛋白质需求。

q.s: Damaged tendon tissue is repaired instantly.
q.why: 第三段明确说明修复并非即时完成。
